To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the vocal loudness of five similar groups was significantly different for comfortable loudness and multiples of comfortable loudness and ranges of comfortable loudness.

the vocal loudness behaviors of the groups of speakers differed significantly in comfortable loudness, in loudness at 2x, 3x, 4, 0.5, and 0x comfortable loudness, as well as in the ranges between 4x and 0.25x comfortable loudness; and, interclass reliabilities for the measures were high and significantly different from zero.

the vocal loudness productions of speakers are significantly affected by the speaker’s gender, age, and hearing status; that the comfortable vocal loudness of speakers is significantly affected by the listener’s gender, age and hearing status; and that the comfortable vocal range of speakers is significantly related to the comfortable vocal loudnes of speakers.

the measurement of loudness behaviors.
the specification of the vocal loudness behavior of the speaker.

we have developed a set of measures that can be used to characterize vocal loudness behaviors of speakers.
vocal loudness is not a unitary construct, but a complex one that can be described in terms of a set of related behaviors that are not independent of one another.
